name: LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS ClarityOp Surgical Ocular
description:
The ClarityOp is a medically licensed full ocular replacement designed specifically for surgical and diagnostic professionals, offering variable focal depth from 0.1mm macro-resolution to standard distance vision in a single continuous zoom. The implant overlays tissue-type differentiation, subsurface vein mapping, and real-time vitals pulled from a patient's biometric feed directly onto the surgeon's visual field. A proprietary biocompatible ceramic housing and Lazarus's rejection-suppression coating make this one of the safest full-eye replacements on the market.

The ClarityOp is the standard of care at Meridian's Spire-tier hospitals and is increasingly common among trauma surgeons working in Rack-district urgent care centers who need to stretch every resource. Medical students who can afford the implant early in their training report dramatically accelerated skill development, creating quiet controversy about the ethics of augmentation-assisted licensure.
installation_requirements: Licensed medical facility; pre-op ocular nerve mapping; Lazarus-certified installation only for warranty validity
rejection_risk: Low — Lazarus biocompatible ceramic housing and rejection-suppression coating reduce immune response significantly
maintenance: Annual recalibration at Lazarus-certified clinic; diagnostic overlay database updated quarterly via encrypted medical network
side_effects: Involuntary diagnostic overlay activation in social settings — users report being unable to stop analyzing the vasculature of faces during conversation
Extended macro-focus use causes mild nausea during readjustment to normal focal distances
Hyper-awareness of biological imperfection in self and others; associated with elevated rates of body dysmorphia in long-term users
MedNet wireless connection creates minor vulnerability to medical network intrusion
cultural_context: ClarityOps are a quiet status marker in Meridian's medical community — their faint pale-blue scleral tint is recognizable to anyone who spends time in hospital corridors. Outside of medicine, they've found an unlikely secondary market among high-end tattoo artists, watchmakers, and artisan cyberlimb builders who need the same precision optics. Lazarus maintains tight licensing controls, but the medical-community black market for expired or transferred units is an open secret.
story_hooks: A surgeon's ClarityOp recorded everything during a procedure on a high-profile patient — someone wants that visual memory extracted before it's overwritten
Counterfeit ClarityOps are appearing on the Shelf market, visually identical but lacking the tissue-differentiation overlay — surgeons are performing procedures with false confidence
A retired surgeon refuses to have her ClarityOps removed despite a terminal rejection cascade — she claims she needs to see clearly for one last job
